title: The Man Who Jumped Out Of A Plane
sources: FBI, 'D.B. Cooper Hijacking' (fbi.gov/history): Nov 24, 1971, Northwest Orient Flight 305, Portland to Seattle; ticket bought as 'Dan Cooper'; note to a flight attendant; $200,000 and four parachutes; passengers released in Seattle; jumped from the rear stairs; $5,800 found in 1980; active investigation suspended in 2016
History.com, 'Who Was the Mysterious Hijacker D.B. Cooper?'

lines.text: A quiet man in a dark suit boards a flight to Seattle.
The name on his ticket is Dan Cooper.
Mid-flight, he hands the flight attendant a note.
He wants two hundred thousand dollars, and four parachutes.
In Seattle, he lets every passenger go.
Then, somewhere over the dark forests of Washington, in the rain,
he opens the rear stairs, and jumps.
Nine years later, a boy found some of the cash buried by a river.
lines.caps: Nine years *later, | a *boy found | some of the *cash.

lines.text: The rest of it, and Dan Cooper, are still missing.
